smoking_behavior.quit_intention: Will quit in the next month

rated_messages.input_message: Feelings aren't permanent. They are always changing like the weather. Observe the storm that is coming, but don't fight it. Eventually the weather will change.

To keep on track, small changes can really help. For example, keep a list of quit reasons where you used to keep cigarettes, rearrange your living space, or grab some extra pens to fiddle with to keep your hands busy.
Setting small goals when you feel unmotivated is best. Maybe a small goal for now is to breathe deeply for the next 3 minutes instead of smoking.
Tell yourself, “I am going to quit smoking soon.” Say it out loud. Say to yourself, “I am too strong to continue smoking for the rest of my life."

Spend 3 minutes noticing how your hands feel, how your mouth feels, and how your chest feels. The more you practice noticing these things without smoking, the sooner this place will stop being a trigger for you.
No need to get rid of these feelings or control them with a smoke. They are not permanent.
It's normal to have some doubts during a quit attempt. Keep your quit reasons on hand to remind yourself if ever you feel uncertain or undecided.
Notice what it feels like to see other people smoke and choose not to smoke. Notice what thoughts or emotions come up. Allow them to come and go. They will pass and so will this urge.
Imagine this urge as just another backseat passenger that hopped in after seeing other people smoke. You are the driver and you still get to call the shots.
If leaving social situations to avoid smokers feels awkward, make sure you have something to do instead - take sugar free mints, lollipops or low fat snacks to chew, or use a stress ball.
